newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss hotel bookings fall in 1996 for sixth year.
newsitem.headline: Swiss hotel bookings fall in 1996 for sixth year.

text.p: Switzerland's weak economy took another blow when hotel stays, a key indicator for the tourism sector, fell last year for the sixth year in a row to the lowest level since 1965, the Federal Statistics Office said.
Overnight stays in 1996 dropped 4.8 percent or 1.5 million from the year before to 29.7 million.
Bookings by foreign visitors were down more strongly by 6.0 percent to 17.3 million while hotel stays by Swiss fell 3.2 percent to 12.4 million.
"Demand therefore reached the lowest level since 1965," the office said in a statement.
It blamed sluggish economies in Europe, weak domestic demand in Switzerland after six years of virtually zero growth, a strong Swiss franc exchange rate for much of 1996 and foreign competition.
The office said an increase in December of 2.8 percent, the first monthly rise in four years, was not enough to offset the decline that has continued since a record year in 1990.

Economists say tourism accounts for about seven percent of Swiss Gross Domestic Product (GDP), which has been stagnant overall since 1991 and is widely projected to grow by less than one percent in 1997.
